The signed middleware only authenticates the URL and checks its expiry; it does not make the request single-use.
`UnsubscribeController` toggles the flag:
```php
'marketing_opt_in' => ! $user->marketing_opt_in
```
So the first request changes `true → false`, while a replay changes `false → true`. It also sends `UnsubscribeConfirmed` on every request, causing duplicate emails.
The fix is to make the mutation one-way:
```php
$user->update(['marketing_opt_in' => false]);
```
Send confirmation only once. For strict “once per signed-link lifetime,” persist an idempotency record keyed by the signed URL/signature with a unique constraint, and atomically claim it before sending. This also handles simultaneous scanner requests safely. The existing route, URL format, and `signed` middleware can remain unchanged.
<diagnosis>
The unsubscribe controller treats a valid signed unsubscribe URL as a toggle rather than a one-way command. Replaying the same still-valid URL therefore changes `marketing_opt_in` from false back to true, while the unconditional mail call sends a confirmation on every replay. Keep the signed route and middleware, always set `marketing_opt_in` to false, and gate confirmation dispatch behind an atomic persisted idempotency key derived from the signed link so each link lifetime can produce exactly one confirmation.
</diagnosis>
